review_notes: Reviewed all of lines 1–152 and inspected the imported TensorDivision source for the restriction-functor composition pattern. The proposed simplification uses only the existing functoriality and category-associativity rewrites; I have not tested or compiled it.

findings.excerpt:
have composition :
      (unitIso.inv ≫ restriction.map s) ≫ restriction.map g.hom ≫ f.hom =
        (unitIso.inv ≫ restriction.map (s ≫ g.hom)) ≫ f.hom := by
    calc
      _ = unitIso.inv ≫ (restriction.map s ≫ restriction.map g.hom) ≫ f.hom :=
        (Category.assoc _ _ _).trans
          (congrArg (fun morphism => unitIso.inv ≫ morphism)
            (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm)
      _ = unitIso.inv ≫ restriction.map (s ≫ g.hom) ≫ f.hom :=
        congrArg (fun morphism => unitIso.inv ≫ morphism ≫ f.hom)
          (restriction.map_comp s g.hom).symm
      _ = _ := (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm
findings.problem: The composition equality is proved with three calc steps that manually reassociate morphisms around the single substantive fact, `restriction.map_comp`. This obscures the straightforward functoriality argument and leaves avoidable associativity bookkeeping.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the `by` block proving `composition` with `by
    simp only [Category.assoc, restriction.map_comp]`. This normalizes the associations and rewrites the composite of mapped morphisms directly, leaving the reason the equality holds visible in the rewrite list.
findings.benefit: Readers can see immediately that the equality follows from functoriality of restriction and associativity, without tracing several reassociation steps. The key mathematical idea is at least as clear, and the later use of this equality is unchanged.
